blockAssessments.assessment: Paragraph 1 retains mobile electrons and ions, positive/negative charge balance over a sufficiently large region, electric-field interaction, and collective response. It distinguishes approximate overall electrical neutrality from absence of charge carriers. Paragraph 2 explicitly does not require every small region to be exactly neutral and allows both fully ionized two-component and partially ionized multicomponent systems. Paragraph 3 correctly names the neutral-particle-containing case partially ionized plasma, with coherent strong emphasis.

Paragraph 4 limits excess positive charge and failure of approximate charge cancellation to some regions near the cathode. Paragraph 5 says those regions cannot themselves be treated as approximately neutral plasma regions, not that every nonquasineutral region is categorically excluded from all plasma physics. It identifies the positive column and faithfully preserves the original terminology explanation. Paragraph 6 gives the positive column as an example of gas-discharge plasma.

Paragraph 7 retains gas-discharge plasma in neon lamps and fluorescent tubes, transfer of discharge energy to particles, and subsequent radiation. Paragraph 8 correctly locates phosphors on the inner glass surface, distinguishes their absorption of plasma radiation from their emission of visible light, and scopes near-white output to appropriate phosphor selection. Heading and sentences are readable and correctly marked.

Paragraph 9 preserves gas lasers as an application, discharge energy transfer to the gas, laser light, directional radiation, and later optics context. Paragraph 10 makes power depend on particular design and expressly rejects the claim that use of gas alone makes a laser the most powerful light source.

Paragraph 11 retains mobile electrons and positive ion cores in liquid and solid metals. Paragraph 12 defines the ion core and preserves approximate overall charge balance; its semicolon joins clauses within the same paragraph. Paragraph 13 explicitly treats electron plasma as a collective-motion model, not an ionized-gas description of solid metal, and places usual crystal ion cores near fixed lattice positions with local vibrations rather than free motion through the solid. Paragraph 14 distinguishes gas-discharge plasma and liquid metals without fixed crystal lattice positions and retains the density range. Paragraph 15 explains particles per unit volume and per cubic centimeter. Paragraph 16 retains the need for quantum mechanics at high density and rejects unchanged use of dilute-gas laws.

The astronomical heading and paragraph retain high temperatures and ionizing radiation in stars such as the Sun, electron loss from atoms, and much stellar matter in a plasma state. The English does not claim that all astronomical matter is fully ionized.

Paragraph 18 scopes electrons, ions, and bare positive atomic nuclei to the ionized interstellar component, and preserves very low density without universally low temperature. Paragraph 19 explicitly describes temperature variation, including warmer ionized gas and very hot plasma, and says low density alone does not establish cold plasma.

The paragraph retains continuing stellar energy release, the need to replenish internal energy, thermonuclear reactions combining light nuclei into heavier nuclei, energy release, the term nuclear fusion, and support of high-temperature stellar plasma. Strong terms are correctly delimited.

Paragraph 21 describes terrestrial controlled fusion as research and an energy prospect, distinguishes achieving a reaction from a practical energy-producing system, and retains sustained operation, fuel supply, materials, and whole-system energy balance conditions. Paragraph 22 expressly rejects describing the prospect as an inexhaustible energy source already achieved.

conditionChecklist.condition: Approximate large-region charge balance, charged particles, and collective electric-field response; not pointwise exact neutrality.
Nonquasineutral cathode-region statement is limited to treatment as approximately neutral plasma regions, not categorical exclusion of all plasma.
Fluorescent phosphors absorb plasma radiation and emit visible light; appropriate selection produces near-white output.
No strongest-gas-laser or gas-alone highest-power claim.
Solid ion cores occupy usual lattice positions; conduction electrons are mobile, while liquid-metal ion cores are not fixed at those crystal positions.
Electron-plasma treatment of metal is a collective model, not a claim that solid metal is ionized gas.
Density range and particles-per-cubic-centimeter meaning are retained exactly; dense-electron description remains quantum rather than unchanged dilute-gas laws.
Low interstellar density does not imply uniformly low temperature; ionized components and regional temperature variation remain scoped.
Stellar thermonuclear fusion supplies energy; terrestrial research prospects are not achieved inexhaustible practical power.
